What says Uluma-e-Karam in the light of Quran-o-Sunnah: There is a practice in our area according to which Nikah is done in proper Islamic way at the time of engagement but at the time of rukhsati, again Nikah is done in the same way. Uluma doing so admit the fact that once Nikah is done at the time of engagement, it is not necessary to repeat it at the time of rukhsati however they says it is better to repeat it ( or renew it ) at the time of rukhsati. It is necessary to mention here that it is an integaral part of the marriage ceremony in our area to arrange a function of doing nikah on the evening of Shabe-uroosi in which all close relatives participate. So if this function is not done, there would be confusion in the mind of relatives. My question is: ? whether this practice of repeating nikah is according to Quran-o-Sunnah and is there any evidence available in Sunnah. ? Is there any Hadees proving that this practice is forbidden. ? Then in case there is no evidence available in Sunah regarding allowing or disallowing, whether one can be allowed to repeat nikah for the sake of making people?s mind clear. 3765 views Q. answer: Social Matters >> Nikah (Marriage) Question ID: 48061 Country: India Title: Nikah Question: One woman got married 5 years back. But her husband has gone missing from last 2 years. Now is it allowed in Shariah for that woman to get remarried? If it is allowed then after how many years? How many years would she wait for her husband? Answer ID: 48061 Posted on: Sep 1, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 1358/L-462/TL=11/1434) In the above mentioned case, if the husband of the said woman is missing in a way that nothing is known about his death or life then the woman should file her case in Shariah Panchayat. If the Shariah Panchayat after searching the missing husband nullifies the nikah as per the guidelines of Al-Heelah Al-Najizah then the woman may marry anywhere after passing her iddah. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
